{{Quote|Mos Eisley Spaceport. You will never find a more wretched hive of scum and villainy. We must be cautious.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], to [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
'''Mos Eisley''' ([[Wikipedia:International Phonetic Alphabet for English|pronounced]] /mɑs aɪzliː/, ''moss izelee'', {{C|{{Audio|MosEisleySpaceport.flac|Listen}}}}), also known as '''Mos Eisley Spaceport''', formerly known as '''Eisley''', was a large [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] town on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. It was the largest settlement on the planet and generally known as the "armpit of the galaxy."

==Description==
{{Quote|Mos Eisley is known as the galaxy's armpit. I guess there are worse parts of the anatomy where we could be stuck.|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]|<ref name="Shadows of the Empire (novel)">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>}}
[[File:MosEisleyFarFarAway-ANH.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The full expanse of Mos Eisley]]
Mos Eisley was located on a plain<ref name="ANH novel">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars: A New Hope'' novelization]]</ref> in a valley to the east of the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]], and roughly 80 kilometers north of [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]], near the desert [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt]]. It could be reached from the high ground to the west via the [[Sluuce Canyon/Legends|Sluuce Canyon]].<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" />

From a distance, the spaceport appeared as a haphazard collage of low-grade concrete, stone, [[Plastoid/Legends|plastoid]],<ref name="ANH novel" /> and [[Pourstone/Legends|pourstone]]<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> structures that spread outward from a central power and water distribution plant with the appearance of a spoked wheel. A portion of the city lay underground, including launch stations:<ref name="ANH novel" /> Though the city lacked a main landing facility, it relied on 362 individual [[Hangar/Legends|hangars]].<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /><ref name="BtMF1">[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 1|''Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon'' 1]]</ref> By order of the Empire, all of these hangars were equipped with [[time-lock device]]s.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> Illegally parked vessels were not an uncommon sight.

The buildings were designed to provide protection from the twin suns, and though they had primitive outer appearances, many old-stone buildings had [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] double walls with circulating coolant flowing between.<ref name="ANH novel" />

It had a population of around 40 to 60 thousand people, varying seasonally.

Streets in the city included Corporation Road, Curved Street, [[Outer Curved Street/Legends|Outer Curved Street]], [[Straight Street/Legends|Straight Street]], [[Spacers Row/Legends|Spacers Row]], [[Paradise Road/Legends|Paradise Road]], [[Dune Street/Legends|Dune Street]], and [[Kerner Plaza/Legends|Kerner Plaza]]. Many citizens rode [[Ronto/Legends|rontos]], [[Dewback/Legends|dewbacks]], and other beasts of burden.

[[File:Mos_Eisley_spaceship.png|thumb|right|250px|The streets of Mos Eisley]]
Mos Eisley was divided into the "[[New Quarter/Legends|New Quarter]]" and the "[[Old Quarter/Legends|Old Quarter]]." The Old Quarter was originally wheel-shaped and contained a thriving marketplace. Jabba the Hutt also maintained a residence there, known as the [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|Desilijic Complex]], since it was difficult to make business from his palace. The New Quarter was more tourist-friendly and was a merchant district where tourists could relax (though there was still much crime). [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] served as the hub of the newer quarter.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> Each quarter had individual neighborhoods, such as the rough-and-tumble [[Tar Mass]] area.

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Empire established a small [[Imperial garrison base|garrison]] in Mos Eisley, although this did not help with the city's massive crime rates. The base was located near the cantina and whenever an expansion was required, the Empire would simply level surrounding buildings.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> To support the constant flow of [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]], Mos Eisley featured a large number of hotels, [[Casino/Legends|casinos]], and [[Cantina/Legends|cantinas]].

The shops district was close to a hangar, the markets, a warehouse, and a housing complex.<ref name="BFI">[[Star Wars Battlefront: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|The city's history actually has a lot to do with a crashed starship, the Dowager Queen, which crashed into the desert flats in the center of what is now the city of Mos Eisley.|[[Mayor/Legends|Mayor]] [[Mikdanyell Guh'rantt]], to a spacer|<ref name="SWG:MMG">{{SWGcite|exp=RotW|type=conversation|Mayor Mikdanyell Guh'rantt|Tatooine}}</ref>}}
[[File:Mos_Eisley_street.png|thumb|left|250px|The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] presence in Mos Eisley in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]]]]
Mos Eisley was built with commerce in mind.<ref name="ANH novel" /> It was founded as a substitute for the nearby, yet more expensive, [[Anchorhead/Legends|Anchorhead]]. Located around the crash site of the [[Dowager Queen/Legends|''Dowager Queen'']], the survivors of this crash originally named it simply Eisley. They later renamed it to fit with other towns such as [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] and [[Mos Gamos]]. These same immigrants would later found the planet's future capital, [[Bestine (city)/Legends|Bestine]].

The city was reputed to be a hub for shady persons and illegal activity, notably the smuggling of spice and illegal arms. The city did not have enough customs officers to keep up with the crime, and even when criminals were caught, they often successfully bribed the officers.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations" /> Jabba the Hutt owned a [[Desilijic Complex/Legends|townhouse]] in the city.

Because Tatooine was a desert planet, availability of water was at a premium and the sewers were very small. To reprocess water quickly, it was decided that the sewers should use a [[Bunkurd Reclamation System]]. Unfortunately, it was prone to leaking and often led to [[Bunkurd Sewer Disorder]], which native [[Falynn Sandskimmer]] once contracted as a youth.

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the "hive of scum and villainy" became a target of notorious [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] officer [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], who had been tasked with controlling the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] by [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] prior to the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. He began his conquest on the outskirts of Mos Eisley, seeing the city as an ideal outpost for their operations. Unfortunately for the Imperials, the Rebel Alliance had their own outpost station in nearby Anchorhead, and moved to intercept the Empire, thus the [[Battle of Tatooine (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Tatooine]] ensued. Though the Empire emerged victorious from the desert battle, their task force was considerably diminished, and their eventual presence in Mos Eisley was less than had been expected. This came back to haunt the Empire, as [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] slipped through the cracks in what would otherwise have been a mighty security force. The Rebel presence in Mos Eisley was finally routed during the latter part of the battle.

[[File:MosEisley-celebration.png|thumb|right|200px|The streets of Mos Eisley erupted in celebration at the news of the Emperor's demise.]]
[[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina/Legends|Chalmun's Cantina]] played a crucial role in these times, as the establishment was where [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] met [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] in their quest to get to [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] in order to deliver the [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]] to the Alliance. The Imperials also searched Mos Eisley for R2-D2 and C-3PO, the holders of the missing [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] plans.<ref name="ANH" />

Shortly thereafter, Mos Eisley was transformed overnight into a police state run by the Empire as a direct result of the Battle of Yavin. In addition, it suffered from a severe outbreak of [[Bledsoe's disease]] after a Jawa that unknowingly took a transport capsule from a crash site containing squills died within the cantina. Luke Skywalker reluctantly [[Mission to Tatooine (Luke Skywalker)|returned]] to Tatooine in order to investigate the capsule.<ref name="Tatooine Sojourn">"[[Tatooine Sojourn]]"</ref>

Six months later,<ref name="RS I guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> Mos Eisley was [[Ambush at Mos Eisley|attacked]] by Imperial [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE Bombers]] and [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]] to draw out the now&ndash;[[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] Luke Skywalker.<ref name="RSI">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref> A [[Unidentified bounty hunter (Imperial tip)|bounty hunter]] had provided information which led to the raid.<ref name="RS I guide" />

After the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] [[Mikdanyell Guh'rantt]] was the [[Mayor/Legends|mayor]] of Mos Eisley. During his term, Guh'rantt was willing to improve, despite limited funding, life conditions and security in the city. To achieve those objectives, he worked closely with the animal control [[Officer/Legends|officer]] [[Entha Kandela]], the veteran [[Sniper/Legends|marksman]] [[Purvis Arrison]] and the combat expert [[Peawp R'dawc]], and he occasionally hired [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] to assist them. However, the mayor eventually found himself indebted to the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]].<ref name="SWG:IiH">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|If It Helps|Tatooine}}</ref> In retaliation for the late payments, Jabba developed a plan to trick the [[Tusken Raider/Legends|Tusken Raiders]] into attacking Mos Eisley. One of Jabba's minions, the [[Trandoshan/Legends|Trandoshan]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], recruited a spacer to attack Tuskens around Mos Eisley so they would think the [[Tatooine militia|Mos Eisley militia]] was responsible. Although a Tusken berserker discovered the truth and was promptly assassinated by the spacer, Jabba's plan eventually worked out.<ref name="SWG:TR">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=general|Tusken's Rage|Tatooine}}</ref> Then, hostile Tuskens began to amass in [[Junktown]], a slum on the outskirts of Mos Eisley, to attack the city.<ref name="SWG:TRiME">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Tusken Raiders in Mos Eisley|Tatooine}}</ref> Fortunately, in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref> [[Bib Fortuna/Legends|Bib Fortuna]], Jabba's [[Majordomo/Legends|majordomo]], offered the services of spacers to help the mayor find a way to reimburse the Hutt.<ref name="SWG:IiH" /> Working with Peawp R'dawc, the spacers defeated undesirable thugs and criminals who prowled around Mos Eisley.<ref name="SWG:NR">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|No Respect!|Tatooine}}</ref><ref name="SWG:MT">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Moisture Thieves|Tatooine}}</ref><ref name="SWG:ROtG">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Run Out the Gunrunners|Tatooine}}</ref><ref name="SWG:IT">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Identity Theft|Tatooine}}</ref> In addition, the spacers and Entha Kandela eliminated various creatures which were posing a threat to public health and damaging city infrastructure.<ref name="SWG:GmSS">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Give me Some Skin|Tatooine}}</ref><ref name="SWG:BH">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Bug Hunt|Tatooine}}</ref><ref name="SWG:DB">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Dem Bones|Tatooine}}</ref><ref name="SWG:RT">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Rill Thing|Tatooine}}</ref><ref name="SWG:MM">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Mighty Mites|Tatooine}}</ref> Finally, the spacer under the orders of Purvis Arrison battled the Tusken Raiders around Junktown. The adventurers killed enough Tuskens to preventing them to raid Mos Eisley for the time being.<ref name="SWG:TI">{{SWGcite|exp=NGE|type=class|Legacy|Tusken Infestation|Tatooine}}</ref>

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], Mos Eisley and other communities on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] were put under Imperial curfew by a [[Unidentified Moradmin Bast look-alike|nameless Moff]]. [[Ackmena/Legends|Ackmena]], the night bartender of Chalmun's Cantina, was the one to receive the message, and reluctantly responded by [[Goodnight, But Not Goodbye/Legends|singing]] to encourage her guests to leave.<ref name="Holiday">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref>

In [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the city erupted in celebrations after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|destruction]] of the Empire's [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] and the death of the Emperor.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-moseisley.png|thumb|right|200px|Concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]]]
The real-world locations for ''Mos Eisley'' are mostly in [[Djerba]], [[Tunisia]] with the establishing shot on Dante's View in Death Valley looking toward Furnace Creek.

Mos Eisley appears in a map in the [[2004]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront]]''. During the Historical Campaign, the battle on the map appears as an Imperial mission, although the game's story is [[Canon|secondary continuity]], according to [[Leland Chee]], the keeper of [[Lucasfilm]]'s [[Holocron continuity database]].<ref name="Blog">{{Blog|holocron|56|starwars.com forum HolocronKeeper comments archive}}</ref> Also, Mos Eisley was used as a map for ''Star Wars: Battlefront''{{'s}} successor, ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', where the player could play as either a hero or a villain.

Mos Eisley appears in the training missions in the [[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (series)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']] video game series.
